test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 13 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: 731 metallic cubes with a side length of 3.6 cm are available to be melted and formed into a machine part consisting of two solid cones with a base radius of 5.4 cm, joined at their bases. The heights of the cones are 49 cm and 35 cm, respectively. How many cubes will be surplus after the formation of the two cones? (Take π = 3.14)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume of 1 **cube** = 3.6³ = 46.656 cm³

Volume of **machine part** = (1/3) × 3.14 × 5.4² × (49 + 35) = 2563.9104 cm³

Number of **cubes used** = 2563.9104 ÷ 46.656 = 55

**Surplus cubes** = 731 − 55 = 676

**∴ The correct answer is 676 cubes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total cubes = 731, **Side** (a) = 3.6 cm, **Radius** (r) = 5.4 cm, **Heights** (h₁, h₂) = 49 cm, 35 cm, π = 3.14

**Formula Used:** Volume of cube = a³; Volume of cone = (1/3)πr²h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/92007154812e1ebf7b7a3fad674decb23c53f3434faf6ade95de1e21ffbd49a0.png] 

⇒ Volume of 1 **cube** = 3.6 × 3.6 × 3.6 = 46.656 cm³

⇒ Total volume of **machine part** = (1/3) × π × r² × h₁ + (1/3) × π × r² × h₂

⇒ Volume = (1/3) × 3.14 × (5.4)² × (49 + 35)

⇒ Volume = (1/3) × 3.14 × 29.16 × 84

⇒ Volume = 3.14 × 29.16 × 28 = 2563.9104 cm³

⇒ Number of **cubes used** (n) = Total Volume ÷ Volume of 1 cube

⇒ n = 2563.9104 ÷ 46.656 = 55

⇒ **Surplus cubes** = Total cubes − Cubes used = 731 − 55 = 676

**∴ The correct answer is 676 cubes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of Solid Figures

For a **cone**, Volume = (1/3)πr²h. For a **cube**, Volume = a³. When melting and recasting, the total volume remains constant.

Surplus Calculation

Surplus = Total Available Units − Units Utilized. Utilized units must be an integer if discrete items (like cubes) are used.</p
